recent_decisions.decision: THE FAR RUNG DESIGN (perf arc increment 4, the orbit speckles) went through a 5-agent panel (3 diagnoses + contract + adversarial critique, 1.27M tokens, 86 min) and the critique returned NEEDS_REVISION with 8 blockers, so the implementers were NOT launched on the v1 contract. Diagnosis of record: the speckles are the constructed bodies (cloud_v2_body) point-sampled at footprints 2 to 20x their size (CLOUD_V2_FADE_LO/HI 3.9/4.0 keeps them at full weight under 15 km footprints); the noise body is already band-limited by its mip chain, the built body has no prefiltered representation. The far rung = a planet-fixed PROFILE (per lattice cell and height bin: cloud fraction f and mean density G of the same field the march renders) in an RGBA8 atlas of six nested windows + one global equirect map with mips, read by lodb, integrated in transmittance by a clumped-medium element law (fraction + in-cloud density; a plain mean fed to Beer-Lambert is the white-veil class), skipping density AND the sun ladder at w=1. Blockers found by the critique and the orchestrator's v2 decisions (scratchpad farrung-amendments.md, folded into docs/design/cloud-far-rung.md by a revision agent): (B1) the bake cost was understated ~100x (uncached SDF point tests per texel: a level-5 bake ~2.8 s, the global ~85 s) -> A1 analytic per-cloud ellipses from a runtime CALIBRATION table (canonical archetype cross-section radius + mean density baked once from the shipped SDF), cell-stratified ellipse tests at fine levels; (B2) the element law was not step-invariant (ln T ~ seg^2) -> A7 tau_elem = sigma D L_elem, T = pow(1 - w f (1 - e^-tau_elem), seg/L_elem), with a prove-red on eco 0 vs 1; (B3) the shell draw's group 3 binding 0 is the temporal accumulation map, so the profile's group cannot carry the sun atlas there -> A8 a b14 override on the albedo-group builder, every group variant rebuilt; (B4) map_diag 1 writes OPAQUE greyscale, alpha is always 1, so three gates would have passed vacuously -> A9 luminance thresholds, calibrated red on v0.1288 first; (B5) the G5 speckle target (50) was below the metric's no-cloud floor (263) -> A10 at or below High's own count (252) and mass (0.152%) on the map_diag 1 render, and the census promoted to scripts/cloud-speckle-census.js (reproduces every baseline: eco0 2464, eco1 2989, High 252, off 263); (B6) albedo_sampler mip filter is Nearest -> A11 manual two-mip lerp on the global; (B7) the point estimator stratified over the cloud's box, so fine texels were coin flips and a_i was unbounded -> A1's inversion + clamp; (B8) no polar behaviour and no polar fixture -> A4 an ABSOLUTE equal-angle equirect lattice (no cos(lat0) scaling, no anchor) that degrades to the global's mips near the poles, plus a polar fixture and a truncation counter. Warnings adopted: A5 TOROIDAL clipmap windows (each level scrolls by whole cells, the exposed column baked the same frame; the re-anchor full-bake spike and its hysteresis are gone), A6 TIME-based refresh (2 s per level, 60 s global) gated on the MAX of gpu.cloud_profile over a moving fixture, A12 G1 floors per cloud_res arm (693/347/173 km), A13 the level walk + a non-radial instrument for the Chebyshev hand-off square, A14 the column C stored (3 column slices per level: atlas 6144x3584), A15 cloud_res pinned per fixture (the rig config drifted to 2), A16 G4-vs-High reported not gated, A17 an integration stub (constants + a synthetic-pattern bake + stub tap) committed to main BEFORE the implementers start so neither waits on the other, A18 seam scans by image coordinate.
recent_decisions.why: The design's worth is in what the implementers cannot see from their own side: shared layouts, the cost model, and gates that cannot pass on the bad build. The critique reproduced the census numbers itself and found three gates that would have been green on today's speckled picture; launching two implementers on that contract would have produced a merge that looked proven and was not. The amendments are decisions, not a menu, so the revision produces one coherent v2 rather than v1 plus a patch list.

recent_decisions.decision: THE OPERATOR'S F10 TEST REPORT ON v0.1289 (Ultra preset, half res, live toggling, ten screenshots). With in-cloud light on clouds seem to almost become completely transparent as the horizon become very easy to see' (the Eddington experiment, default off); (5) 'With warp band off I see a lot more clouds. With it on it seems like most distant clouds vanish' (2.2 km above a deck; the default is ON since v0.1272); (6) 'I notice zero difference with the field walls on or off' (the null instrument confirmed null). Plus a UI request: the F10 panel is now too long to see; make it a scrollable LEFT SIDEBAR, F10 frees the cursor (no alt-hold), a collapse button on its right edge. ORCHESTRATOR READING: (2) is the sun-shadow cache WINDOW (48.6 km fine / 97 km coarse, planet-fixed so it reads as a rotated square): inside it samples read the baked ladder (real in-cloud sun columns, dark bases), outside they read the v0.1288 analytic column (CLOUD_LC_FAR_ANALYTIC = 1.0), which under-shadows a broken cumulus field (a mean-density slant column is far thinner than the in-cloud column: Jensen), so the far field is too bright and the window edge is the seam; the v0.1288 'look identical' check was made only at rain-26km-nadir, a stratiform case where mean and in-cloud agree. Shipped default, top fix. (1) is the deep relaxation starting at trans 0.5 (half the pixel's light still to come) compounding along long horizon slants; the economy's own rule is no look change and it was never measured on a horizon look at half res. (5) is coverage decaying with distance under the band-limited warp (a thresholded band-limited field loses its mean: the same Jensen class the far rung is designed around), so the DEFAULT loses distant clouds. (3) the anchored march is most likely the physically right one (the old march under-counted extinction to first order in h, v0.1271 assessment); the check is for any double counting. (4) the experiment couples alpha to the light source, which it must not; fix or delete. DISPATCHED: workflow wf_de0676a5 (operator-report-v1289): per finding diagnose -> adversarial verify -> implement in a worktree if confirmed and bounded -> review -> repair; the F10 sidebar implemented in parallel (SidePanel::left + ScrollArea, F10 frees the cursor via the existing grab mechanism, collapse tab on the right edge, headless snapshot). Merges are serial (three fixes may touch 40-clouds.wgsl in disjoint regions) and every fix is gated on the rig with the operator's config once their instance exits (one GPU).
recent_decisions.why: The operator's eye found a shipped-default artifact (the square) that every rig gate missed because the gates were pointed at nadir, in-deck and stratiform vantages, never at a broken cumulus field from 37 km; and a coverage-with-distance defect in a v0.1272 default that the descent-ladder gate of the far rung would have caught weeks later. Formalizations beyond the amendments: C_11 is identically zero so its channel carries T (the whole column), columns sqrt-encoded with CLOUD_FR_COL_SCALE 12 (8-bit tau steps of 0.008 at the low end instead of 2.0); a date-line crossing is a full refill (unwrapping the index would drift coarse levels); the dev truncation counter is Rust's analytic estimate (0 on Earth: the equal-angle lattice never reaches the 512 cap). recent_decisions.decision: THE THREE FAR-RUNG G0 DEFECTS DIAGNOSED (panel far-rung-g0-defects, 6 agents, 1.5M tokens, 43 min; every diagnosis met a critic that redid its measurements). D1 (window-edge steps) CONFIRMED: cloud_profile_tap's level walk collapses onto one level ('if (La >= Lb) { Lb = La; wl = 0 }') for every sample outside the finest CONTAINED window, which at 873 km is everything outside level 2's 255 km window; rb is then never fetched and the whole edge weight of La goes to the GLOBAL, so each window's outer 20 percent band is a smoothstep to the 19.55 km pooled map and one pixel past the rim the walk lands on the next level pure: a bright strip then a step (the critic verified the geometry on four rims to within 5 px and the band's alpha excess +5 to +20 percent with an sRGB-decoded same-pixel estimator; the contract itself specifies the collapse at lines 288-293, so the code was contract-faithful and the contract was the defect). Fix part (1), approved: re-walk from La + 1 so the band hands to the next containing level; part (2) (dz_pool for the global's samples) REJECTED by the critic: it would change every pure-global sample's element height and move the whole outer disc. Rig gotcha found: every map_diag channel leaves through the sRGB swapchain, so channel RATIOS must decode sRGB first (raw bytes read L + r(6 - L) with r about 0.5; cloud-profile-compare.js measured the wrong quantity). D2 (in-window grain) REFUTED as diagnosed (the atlas's per-texel cloud-count variance, fix = a family-keyed level floor): the critic's decisive control was already on disk, prof-stepinv-1000-r1-eco0 vs -eco1 (same camera, same FORCED level, same atlas cells, only the step economy differs): census 108 vs 2566 in the nadir crop, so the economy's deep relaxation striding across the thin layer's bin in the profile share is the carrier (the per-pixel sample-height phase the diagnosis dismissed); the level-floor fix would also have handed low-altitude horizon samples to the global. Decision: the profile share is exempt from the relaxation and the footprint floor (scaled by 1 - w_pf). D3 (the marched field empties from above) CONFIRMED and UNDERSTATED: the built layer is based at the SLAB BASE (41-cloud-bodies.wgsl flat base at up_m = 0), the march's final sample lands exactly on that base plane where density is identically 0, and the vertical reject in cloud_v2_body leaves the SDF at its 1e9 sentinel so the stride is inert from above: only the ONE comb sample above m1 can ever find a humilis (hit probability h / 928 = 0.11 to 0.22 per ray at EVERY altitude; step_near 522 m already loses 3x at 12 km), and the found ones are skimmed by the economy floors (mask histogram flat from 64 to 208: genuinely partial alpha). The diagnosis's fix was broken four ways (a non-conservative bound that omitted br, a polluted g_v2_top_m read after the sun ladder, ungated effects at every altitude, a gate whose reference arm rendered nothing at 30 m steps under the 224 cap and whose pass bar sat on an arm the fix could not move). Decision: the corrected fix (the vertical gap to the ADMITTED region as the bound; the in-cloud floor at a quarter of the found cloud's height from a snapshotted top) behind a new dev bit (light2_color.w bit 12, F10 'Built-body top bound'), default OFF until its rebuilt gate passes: uniform 60 m reference march (193 steps), full-res map_diag 1 masks at 250 and 60 km, the fix arm within 2 points of the reference, the reference above 20 points. Workflow far-rung-4b (WGSL + Rust implementers, critics, repair) launched on v0.1292.2.
recent_decisions.why: The G0 captures named the defects and the panel named the carriers, twice against the readers' own stories; a fix built on the refuted D2 story would have bought blur for the wrong carrier, and D3's fix would have shipped ungated at every altitude with a gate that could only go green.

recent_decisions.decision: E1 AND E2 DIAGNOSED (panel far-rung-g1g7-defects, 4 agents, 1.0M tokens, 47 min; each reader met a critic that redid its measurements). E1 (over-coverage): the reader ray-traced the dumped atlas through the shader's own walk and law (pixel correlation 0.99 against the masks) and named two levers: (1) the hand-off weight and tap level read the STEP footprint (foot = max(tm * pix_ang, dt * 0.25); the vertical ceiling grows as 1 / cos on oblique rays and the clear-air stride is uncapped), so the profile fires on samples the pixel never handed off, with est's seg_len making a stride several bins of f on one sample; (2) the element law clamps the vertical element to the bin but leaves the horizontal one unscaled, over-counting slant crossings by dz / L_v (4.13 humilis; about 12 on the Low sheet's pooled bins). The critic PROVED lever 1 independently (same-boot 30 km twins: 52 percent of pixels above 8 where G7 demands bit-exact) but showed it is a SUB-BAND LEAK below about 150 km, inert in the 200 to 620 km band where the pixel term wins the max; showed lever 2 is a real law error but nadir-neutral and so cannot explain the forced-level exhibit (a nadir PEDESTAL of +95 luminance at cover 0.9, and a SIGN FLIP at cover 0.55 type 0.46 where forced level 0 is DARKER than the field); found the tracer's own residual (measured minus shipped-law 13 percent crop, 26 percent nadir) unnamed; and found the brief's ladder coverage numbers unreproducible (the r4 masks read 57/69/86 not 80/89/97; the rise is largely the camera zooming into one weather cell). recent_decisions.decision: THE D3 TOP-BOUND NULL DIAGNOSED (high confidence, third attempt after two usage cutoffs; read-only, measured on the v0.1293 gate captures). The easy explanations are REFUTED by reading the value end to end: cloud_v2_body writes the vertical gap into best and publishes it unconditionally to g_v2_sdf_m BEFORE its early return, the march reads it and converts metres by the same factor the body used (no unit mismatch), and the stride margin is about 265 m against gaps of kilometres (it does not eat the leap). THE REAL MECHANISM, in three parts. (1) The published plane is height * sy + br, where br is a HORIZONTAL cluster bounding radius (hundreds of metres to kilometres): a vertical bound subtracting a horizontal radius, so the leap targets a plane one cluster radius ABOVE a 150 to 400 m cloud and never the cloud. (2) The stride then overrides the base comb: the fix arm marches the whole 11.58 km nadir chord in 8.6 samples (1.35 km a step, ABOVE the 928 m vertical ceiling) against the 60 m reference arm s 192; and on exactly the pixels where the bit LOSES a cloud prod had rendered, the fix arm used FEWER samples than its own average (7.6 against 8.6 at 250 km, 13.0 against 15.1 at 60 km), which is the stride carrying the ray past the layer. (3) The value is published into g_v2_sdf_m, which is deliberately never reset when the body path is skipped (harmless for small near-surface distances, fatal for a kilometre-scale from-above gap), so it leaks into samples that evaluated no body. THE OTHER HALF OF THE BIT WORKS: the in-cloud footprint floor cap makes found clouds render MORE opaque, not thinner (the top alpha band at 60 km, prod 0.55 percent, fix 1.96, reference 3.75), refuting the thinning hypothesis; it should be split onto its own switch. AND THE GATE WAS VOID on its own written preconditions: the reference arm reads 8.55 and 8.35 percent coverage against its own 20-point bar, and at 60 km prod sits 1.24 points below ref against a 4-point requirement, so neither a pass nor a fail was admissible from it; the Sahara camera at cover 0.5 humilis does not put enough cloud in the crop to be a reference. FIX (4d, bounded): drop br from the vertical bound, publish into a distinct global reset every sample, clamp a from-above stride to the vertical ceiling so a miss degrades to today s comb, split the floor cap onto its own bit, and re-cut the fixture onto a cloudier camera with a prod-steps twin.
recent_decisions.why: A null result that had survived two cutoffs turned out to hide one wrong term, one leaked global, one missing clamp and a working half, and a gate that could not have adjudicated any of them.

recent_decisions.decision: CORRECTION plus a real authorization hole found by the recon workflow. THE CORRECTION: my earlier claim that "canonical CBOR is not canonical across clients" is WRONG and is withdrawn. Rust DOES sort map keys: to_canonical_bytes (src/relay/core/encoding.rs:18) calls canonicalize, which sorts at :62-66 by length then bytewise, the identical rule to cborMap in web/shared/canonical-cbor.js:96-108. cbor_map alone is unsorted and its own doc comment says so; payload_cbor routes through the canonical encoder. Multi-key payloads are byte-identical across languages, which is exactly why a browser-built proposal verified on the Rust relay. I read cbor_map and stopped one function short. The wrong claim reached a commit message, PRIORITIES, this journal and the operator, and it told a future session to change a signing byte format that is already correct, which would have broken every client at once. recent_decisions.decision: TYPOGRAPHY, v0.1300.0 to v0.1301.1. The operator asked why the project uses so many different fonts and whether one could be cohesive between web and app, then chose the long-term answer on three criteria: user safety, ease of use, global access. Those pick Noto Sans, whose own stated mission is the same shape as the project's. Two evaluations, 33 agents, full record in docs/design/typography.md. THE DECISIVE FINDING WAS NOT ABOUT TYPEFACES: a 2026 Annals of Dyslexia meta-analysis pooled 15 studies, 91 effect sizes, N=688 on special dyslexia typefaces and found g = -0.04, and Marinus et al. 2016 showed why the folklore survives (Dyslexie beat Arial by 7 percent, then they matched Arial's SPACING to Dyslexie's and the advantage vanished). The benefit is spacing, which is a CSS property and an egui parameter, not a font file. SHIPPED: the 24-word seed phrase was a bare proportional label at 11.9px inside a frame whose own comment calls it the single most dangerous string in the app, while main_menu.rs rendered the same words in monospace 40 lines away; eight character-by-character sites now use Hack, including both base64 invite ticket fields, the only strings in the product where 0, O, I and l coexist. Every arrow in the proportional UI was tofu on Linux and macOS because Ubuntu-Light carries 0 of 112 arrows and epaint puts Hack in Monospace only, while U+2192 appears 111 times in src/gui; Hack is now a computed-position fallback in Proportional and four entries left BROKEN_GLYPHS. set_fonts lived inside the emoji success branch so it never ran at all on a machine with no system emoji font. Japanese and Chinese were tofu since no bundled face has a single CJK codepoint; the system-font probe now covers CJK for zero redistributed bytes. The snapshot rig built bare contexts installing no fonts, so 38 pages had never rendered what a user sees and BROKEN_GLYPHS was partly derived from that. Noto Sans is now the interface face on both surfaces, with 8 self-hosted variable woff2 subsets on web. The web dyslexia toggle was both a placebo (a quarter of the studied dose) and a no-op on Linux and Android (fontconfig ships no Comic Sans metric alias); it is now Reading Comfort at WCAG 1.4.12 doses with word spacing coupled to letter spacing. And the star catalogues were verified CC BY-SA 4.0 from both upstream LICENSE files, making stars.csv and stars.bin a second share-alike source shipping in every release.

recent_decisions.decision: SCHEDULED RE-VOTES, steps 1 and 2 (v0.1302.0, v0.1303.0). The Active focus TIER 0 item, built. A cast vote stays immutable and final; revisiting a question opens a NEW proposal carrying supersedes, so the chain is a real audit trail. Schema: three nullable columns on proposals (review_after, review_cadence_ms, supersedes) read off the CBOR payload, with a cadence and no explicit date implying the first review one cadence after close. Reads: standing_decision walks forward from any link, decision_chain returns the ordered history, proposals_due_for_review is what a scheduler asks for and is already idempotent via NOT EXISTS. GET /api/v2/proposals/{id}/chain exposes it, and ProposalIndex now carries the three fields so a client gets the next-review date without a second request. FIRST, THOUGH: the Active focus block named its own blocker, that web voting is a stub needing canonical-CBOR signing in JS. That is false and was blocking its own item. web/pages/governance.html:482 castVote builds a Dilithium3-signed vote_v1, signs with window.pqSignMessage, posts via window.HumOS.pq.postObject and refreshes the tally, and the KAT is src/relay/core/pq_kat_vote_submission.json. Superseding keeps every decision immutable while still answering what stands now, and it makes reaffirmation visible, which is itself information.

recent_decisions.decision: THE CONSTITUTION IS NOW BUILT FROM THE PARCHMENT, NOT THE HOUSE MANUAL (v0.1306.1). The 8-dimension audit of the shipped Constitution returned 32 confirmed findings. v0.1306 had already fixed the missing signature block and the 41 percent footnote contamination, but five independent dimensions agreed at 3/3 on one it had not: Article I Section 8 shipped with NO granting clause. "The Congress shall have Power" lives in a <chapeau> element and the parser emitted only <clause> children, so the entire enumerated-powers grant was eighteen orphan infinitives with no grantee. Chasing that down condemned the SOURCE: the House Rules and Manual also carried three genuine WORD errors that shipped (Amdt XII "and the number" for "and OF the number"; Amdt XII "in presence" for "in THE presence"; Amdt XVIII "all territorIES" for "all territorY"), 14 manufactured "* * * * * *" elision runs inside complete sentences, and 5 invented bracketed subjects ("[Each House may]") printed as constitutional text. Rebuilt from the National Archives transcriptions of the engrossed parchment plus the Bill of Rights and Amendments XI-XXVII.
recent_decisions.why: The operator asked whether the Constitution we ship is "100% as the founding fathers intended". The House Manual is a working procedural text in which the Constitution is subordinate to its annotations; its editorial design (clause splitting marked with three-star inlines, bracketed subjects supplied so each annotated fragment reads standalone) is incompatible with printing a verbatim Constitution. That is not a transform bug and cannot be patched around, so the source changed. NARA holds the original and states its transcription reflects the parchment's spelling and punctuation, which is why the text now reads "Independance", "In witness whereof", "defence" and "chuse". For the operator's literal question, the parchment is the only honest answer.

recent_decisions.evidence: The pattern held all the way down: every pass found errors in the pass above it. (a) The agent writing the tide guide, reading the locale data to write its own document, found hazards.json calling 11.7 ft the "mean tidal range" TWICE. (b) The phenology agent, having to add the months up to build a calendar, found climate.json claiming "December alone (252 mm) exceeds April through September combined (294 mm)". 252 is less than 294. It also found the "roughly 75 percent" wet-half figure is 79.7 percent by that file's own table. Both were mine. (c) The agent writing hemlock waterparsnip found the water hemlock record DISCLAIMING a field character it had a citation for: USDA ARS says verbatim "side veins of the leaves lead to notches, not to tips at the outer margin", on a page already in that record's own source list. Telling a reader a true character is unsourced trains them to discount it. (d) The phenology agent measured something nobody had: a full year of NOAA CO-OPS predictions for Tracyton, validated against Seattle's published MHHW, showing EVERY daylight minus tide at or below -2.0 ft falls mid-April to mid-August, confirmed across four years. recent_decisions.decision: THE LIBRARY REACHED 46 OF 143 TOPICS WITH A DOCUMENT AND 20 COMPLETE EXPERIENCES (v0.1312.10 to v0.1312.16), AND THE SESSION'S REAL LESSON IS THAT EVERY GUIDE NEEDS AN ADVERSARIAL PASS, NOT JUST THE DATA. Eight guides written by parallel writers against a standing brief that now lives on disk at docs/contributor/library-writer-brief.md instead of being re-derived from memory every wave: the sky as an instrument, how an ecosystem holds together, the climate where you live, pests and disease, hand tools, greywater, taking without ruining it, how plants work, metals and alloys. THREE of them were then put to a critic whose only job was to refute, and all three came back with real defects: 8 in the ecosystem guide, 9 in the sky guide, 9 in the climate guide. The dominant shape is NOT a wrong number. It is a correctly-read source restated with its scope removed: the Forest Service said "in coastal Oregon" and the guide said "the Forest Service records", then told a Kitsap gardener that pH 4.3 was their starting number, which our own soil.json contradicts for half the mapped ground here. Second most common is a claim credited to a source that itself credits somebody else (the land-use correlation is Feist et al., and Scholz et al. says so in its own discussion). Third is a check that cannot fail: the sky guide proved "a full moon is due south at its highest" by sampling 23 minutes after the transit and offering the resulting 8.8 degree miss as confirmation. CONCLUSION FOR FUTURE WAVES: a writer's own confident self-report is not evidence. Budget a refutation pass per guide, not per wave.

recent_decisions.decision: THE IN-WORLD SCREENS LADDER STARTED (six rungs, operator-approved). The operator asked for the native app pages (the real inventory page, not the web page) as touchscreens inside the 3D world, a fixed console room in the home populated by those displays, live feeds and movies on displays, real websites on in-game monitors with affiliate links later, and asked whether to embed VLC or build our own player. Answer executed: our own. The ladder, in build order: (1) ScreenSurface, a persistent offscreen egui context rendered into a wgpu texture that a new unlit material type 24 samples in the PBR shader, driven by a look ray (mouse-look) or the cursor ray (free cursor) turned into synthetic egui pointer events; (2) the screen as a machine def (screen: Some((page, px, face, bezel_m, brightness))) with wall_screen and desk_monitor catalog entries; (3) live feed (MJPEG Watch page on a screen, plus an in-game camera through a render_view_onto refactor of the hires screenshot path); (4) the console room: a room-grade zone type, a rooms.ron join that closes the room_N identity gap, a placed zone in the ship structure; (5) a purpose-built video player (WebM/Matroska + AV1 + Opus, pure-Rust decoders, transcode on ingest) instead of libvlc; (6) the readable web (html5ever parse, egui render, no JavaScript, no Chromium, per decision brief 4) as an OPT-IN default-off AppConfig bool, plus data/web/sites.json, the websites/potential-affiliates database whose embed.status field records the legality of embedding each site (needs_review until a human reads the terms and records basis, terms_url, date, name). Testing uses non-affiliate URLs only. Vocabulary: command deck = the mothership bridge; console room (battlestation) = the home workstation; battlestation is also the device role in device-mesh.md, a different layer. Phase 1 launched as a workflow of four worktree builders (rungs 1+2, 4, 5 core, 6 core), each followed by an adversarial critic and a fix pass; phase 2 (live feed, video and web onto the screens) branches from the merged tree. Also found: data/machines/home.ron, data/blueprints/ship_structure.ron and Cargo.lock had sat uncommitted since 2026-09-08; verified as pure serializer churn (the in-app editor re-sorted the catalog, reformatted floats and wrote CRLF; HEAD holds every def; Cargo.lock only lagged the package version line), so merges may restore those files from HEAD without losing anything.
recent_decisions.why: Operator directive 2026-09-16: "Let's do all 6 rungs and can we test without using affiliate links? We just want to get it working in a basic form. We want to make sure people can actually interact with the web display screen in-game. Then we can figure out the legality of embedding the various platforms. We'll probably want a database for it and for the legality to be mentioned in the database for websites/potential affiliates." The earlier answer established that the engine already had every ingredient (ui_snapshots renders pages offscreen with synthetic clicks; the cloud temporal path binds a render target as an albedo; live_viewer already decodes MJPEG; opus is already compiled in), so this is wiring, not research. Purpose-built player over VLC because libvlc is LGPL with its own render path and we need frames in our texture with royalty-free codecs; readable web over Chromium per Brief 4 and the operator's "our own lightweight browser, not CEF" norm.

recent_decisions.decision: WHERE THE FRAME GOES, MEASURED (operator settings mirrored, planet_clouds false, real GPU timestamp queries, 2560x1387, RTX 4070; 21 boots, 72 cost files; captures in the session scratchpad run1..run9). The clouds are not the cost. (1) The planet: gpu.celestial is the frame and it is per-pixel, independent of geometry: 44.5 ms on the moon with six patches drawn, 61 ms at the 400 km limb, 43 ms in the Sahara at noon; shadows, atmosphere scatter, SSAO, god rays and water FFT move it by nothing; surface-detail octaves are 9 to 11 ms and patch count 17 ms only at grazing ocean views. About 12 ns per pixel at 3.55 Mpx. (2) Forest vantages: Fuji grass underfoot 175 ms; near-tree photoscanned models 68 ms (516 trees within 460 m, budget 260), the cluster-card bake about 38, grass strands 17 (83.6k strands, 7.5 M triangles). (3) Low ocean eyes: the water shell pass gpu.celestial_t 42 to 49 ms, independent of sea state and FFT, only the mesh depth cap moves it. (4) The interior: the opaque pass is about 45 ns per pixel: one flat quad filling the view at 0.3 m costs 160 ms; the console room is 76 to 83 ms of gpu.scene plus 14 of transparent (the glass ceiling); the 211-light untiled loop is 8 ms (lights_tiled off in the operator config); the camera wall adds 17 ms only while its wall is in view (its 10 Hz re-render sums into gpu.scene); the six page surfaces and the video decode cost nothing measurable; home-clock-noon is 19.5 ms versus 18.84 on 09-15. (5) Unattributed: at light vantages 13 to 20 ms per frame with no cpu.frame_total or present-wait timer; no timestamp scope on the screen surface pass, the camera sky pass, the particle compute or the sky-view LUT; nothing splits terrain, trees, grass and bodies inside celestial. (6) Oddities: vsync false in config.json panics deterministically at the first settings apply after world entry (ResizeBuffers invalid call, surface configure "window is in use"); [NearTree] recompute logs every frame while parked; the patch-build log prints the constant 24 instead of the live budget. The F10 sidebar root cause (BUG-076): the HUD allocated a full-screen hover rect and egui 0.31 hit-testing stops at the first covering widget rect regardless of sense, so the sidebar below it was unreachable; fixed in hud.rs with a headless test that fails when the allocation returns; Escape now closes the expanded sidebar first, repeated Escape presses are dropped, and debug/ui_request.json drives the main UI for the rig.
recent_decisions.why: The operator asked where the performance goes with the cloud layer off. The 12 fps is the planet fragment path and, at forest vantages, vegetation; the 9 fps in the console room is the interior opaque fragment cost, not the screens. The fixes are a fragment-cost arc (depth prepass and early-z, tiled lights on, a cheaper terrain fragment path, a near-tree LOD ladder), being designed by a perf-expert pass now; the instrumentation gaps and the camera wall at a quarter of its pixels are being built in a worktree.

Cause: set_vsync reconfigured the surface from the settings-apply block at the tail of the frame arm while that frame's swapchain TextureView was still in scope (DXGI ResizeBuffers 0x887A0001, wgpu "window is in use", fatal). Fix on main (3c932421): the mode is recorded and applied at the next frame's start before the surface texture is acquired; two pure tests; the runtime proof (a rig boot with vsync false reaching the world) is queued behind the P1 boot. UPDATE: the vsync-off boot proof ran on 3c932421: the menu-only boot lived 129 s and the world boot 143 s with zero panics, zero surface errors and frames presented (the rig's own config at vsync false, a real reconfigure scheduled every boot because the surface is created AutoVsync); the negative control, the same rig and config with the pre-fix v0.1314.1 archive, died at 15 s in the menu with the exact BUG-077 panic. The applied present mode is now logged at INFO (4c1f75c6).

Or should we play a video that is stored on my PC? Right now it is just a kinda high pitch sound that keeps looping." Local file: YES, but the player decodes only WebM AV1 + Opus by the codec policy in docs/design/media-player.md (H.264/AAC excluded for patents; VP9/Vorbis not decoded), and there is no in-app way to choose a file. recent_decisions.why: GUI-first: an in-app button that runs ffmpeg under the hood is allowed, a terminal requirement is not. Platform decoders (Media Foundation and friends) remain a later option if ffmpeg-less machines matter.
